comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C83-C94 regarding IRS1/2 recruitment data. Both evaluations strongly support the mechanistic findings showing differential recruitment patterns and competitive inhibition by ΔEx11. OpenEval emphasizes the 'free p85' model consistency, while peer reviewers highlight the abundance of truncated p85α in IRS precipitates even without insulin stimulation.

Perfect agreement on claims C15, C143-C148 regarding the main conclusions. Both evaluations support the dual mechanism (differential activation + dominant negative effect) and recognize this as a significant advance. Peer reviewers describe it as establishing 'a new paradigm' and an 'important study,' while OpenEval notes the tissue-specific balance hypothesis as reasonable speculation requiring further validation.

Strong agreement on claims C73-C82 regarding co-immunoprecipitation data showing differential binding of mutant p85α variants to p110α. Both evaluations support the conclusion that ΔEx11 does not displace endogenous p85α from p110α. OpenEval includes claim C126 not mentioned in peer review, but the core findings are consistently endorsed.

Strong agreement on claims C65-C71 regarding in vitro kinase assay data for SHORT syndrome variants. Both evaluations accept the biochemical findings without challenge. Peer reviewers note the variety of mutational strategies supports the model, while OpenEval acknowledges the mechanistic explanation for tissue-specific phenotypes remains incomplete.

Agreement on claims C10-C11, C50-C54 regarding patient fibroblast data showing reduced p110δ and no PI3K hyperactivation. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval includes additional claims C55, C117-C122 and explicitly notes the single patient limitation, while peer reviewers confirm the findings without emphasizing this limitation in their evaluation.

Agreement on claims C57-C62 regarding dominant negative effects of ΔEx11 overexpression. Both evaluations support the cellular data and conclusions. Peer review includes claims C12-C14 about the study's objectives and findings, while OpenEval includes claims C124-C125 about dose-response analysis. Both emphasize the robust nature of the findings.

Agreement on claims C133-C134 regarding study limitations. Both evaluations acknowledge the single patient limitation and the 3T3-L1 model context. Peer reviewers explicitly state these limitations as UNCERTAIN, requesting investigation of more cell lines, while OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the limitations are appropriately contextualized and do not invalidate findings.
